correctness.rationale: Necessity is derived from the published antitonicity proposition, identity, and semicomplementation. Sufficiency is a complete symbolic reconstruction of (P1)-(P5) for \(A\Rightarrow_N B=N(A\setminus B)\cup(A\cap B)\); the critical (P5) step is \(D\setminus C\subseteq A\setminus H\) for \(D=A\cap B\), \(H=D\Rightarrow_N C\), whence \(N(A\setminus H)\subseteq N(D\setminus C)\subseteq H\). Every coordinate map on the other \(n-1\) atoms is an independent nonzero antitone Boolean function; this gives \((M(n-1)-1)^n\). Double-negation inflation restricts to the previously characterized undirected graph-polarity subfamily. A four-element lattice witnesses the first separation. Direct exhaustive finite checks confirm the full algebra axioms for all realizable unary maps through \(n=3\), and per-coordinate Dedekind counts through \(n=4\); the unrestricted theorem is proved symbolically, not by extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The claim is a complete T-negation reduct classification over finite Boolean lattices and Dedekind-number count, not the older result that F-negations correspond to undirected graph polarities or the classical facts about antitone maps. Chen 2026 defines T and F but does not give this Boolean negation census in inspected algebraic sections. Holliday 2025 treats preconditionals, derived antitone negation and Sasaki/ortholattice, but not this unrestricted T extension principle; the known Sasaki form N(A) union (A intersect B) differs from the displayed N(A\B) lift without involution. Previously published finite-chain classifications do not imply the Boolean case. Related F work has an identical lift formula under stronger reciprocal hypotheses, which the new proof genuinely relaxes with a P5 argument and a new larger cardinality class. Priority risk persists for unlocated protocomplementation extensions.

value.rationale: The unary negation reduct is a natural invariant of the preconditional algebra, and the question asks which weak negations can actually arise from Chen T, not just how many antitone maps exist. The general constructive extension theorem is structurally useful beyond a small census. Counting all realizable negations by Dedekind numbers quantifies the exact gap to the previously classified F graph polarities and locates the first separation on the smallest non-chain bounded lattice. A precise finite Boolean classification can guide semantics, definability, and enumeration of richer conditionals; no unproved applications or paper-sized impact are asserted.
